items.name: &cAlarm
lore: &7Right-click to cycle: off -> alert -> panic -> off

items.name: &eShaft
notes: &fA transmitter: it carries rotation power in a straight line along the axis it points.
&7Produces and consumes nothing on its own — use shafts to route power from a source to a machine.

items.name: &6Gear
notes: &fWorks like a shaft, but also meshes with gears on its perpendicular sides.
&fUse it to turn power around a 90° corner, or to split one input into several directions.
&7Still carries power straight along its own axis, just like a shaft.

items.name: &fOak Gearbox
notes: &fA power hub: couples any aligned shafts or gears on all six faces, passing power and spin through. Sources on different sides never jam; an arm with no source of its own follows the nearest one.
&7Use it to split one input into several directions, or bridge shafts around a corner without a gear's counter-rotation.
&7A frame block like a casing: auto-glues only to SAME-WOOD frame blocks (casings, gearboxes, chassis); brush-glue to pin it to anything else.
&7Comes in every plank wood — the casing in the recipe picks the variant.

items.name: &eChain Pulley
notes: &fA transmitter you can link to other pulleys with a chain.
&7Right-click one pulley with a chain, then another, to link them — uses chains equal to the distance.
&7Power flows only around a closed loop of three or more pulleys, and each link draws a little power.

items.name: &eChain Hoist
lore: &7Pays out chain to raise and lower what hangs beneath
&7Driven by a shaft through it; CW lowers, CCW raises
notes: &fA floor winch: spin it clockwise to pay its chain out downward, anticlockwise to reel it back in.
&7Driven by a shaft running straight through it — the axle lies across your view as you place it, and power carries on to the far side. A wrench reads out its axis.
&7Right-click to open its storage and load it with chains — it spends one chain per block of rope.
&7Whatever sits at the bottom of the chain rides along; with nothing there the chain just extends into the air.
&7Build the platform from Mechanical Casing (or glue) so it moves as one; carried machines keep running.

items.name: &cClutch
notes: &fA shaft you can switch off: give it a redstone signal and it disconnects, stopping power from passing through.
&7With no redstone signal it passes power normally, like a plain shaft.
&7Handy as a clutch/gate to start and stop a branch of your network.

items.name: &dReverser
notes: &fFlips the spin direction when it gets a redstone signal — but stays connected, unlike the clutch which disconnects.
&7Use it to make part of a network turn the opposite way (e.g. to close a door driven by the same source).

items.name: &eRatchet
lore: &7Passes power one way; freewheels when reversed
notes: &fA one-way clutch: it transmits rotation only while the shaft turns its allowed way, and freewheels (disconnects) if the line reverses — the input keeps spinning, the output stops.
&7Wrench to flip the allowed direction (CW/CCW); sneak+wrench to inspect. It adopts the line's current spin when first placed.
&7Freewheel gating is disabled while it rides a moving mechanism (acts as a plain shaft).

items.name: &dRotator
lore: &7Swings blocks glued to it as a door/drawbridge
notes: &fA hinge that swings a structure: on the floor it acts like a door, on a wall like a drawbridge, on a ceiling like a hatch.
&7Carried by another mechanism (e.g. a chain hoist) it keeps its chosen open angle, and any mounted drill/placer/fan keeps aiming the right way as it moves.
&fGlue the blocks you want it to move with the [Glue Brush](mech:glue_item) — any blocks work. With nothing glued it just swings the single block it's attached to.
&fThe network's spin direction decides which way it swings — one direction opens, the other closes.
&7Right-click to cycle how far it opens (90°, 180°, or 270°).

items.name: &bWater Wheel
notes: &fA source worth 2 Power. Mount it on a wall with flowing water touching it, and it spins from the current.
&7Needs flowing water alongside it (its top and sides) to turn — no current, no power. A passive source otherwise (no fuel).

items.name: &4Engine
notes: &fA strong 10-Power source, but it burns fuel — right-click to open its fuel slot.
&fEats the usual furnace fuels: coal, charcoal, blaze rods, lava buckets, logs, planks, sticks, and so on. Higher-value fuels last longer.
&7Puffs smoke while it's running. Can face any direction.

items.name: &5Redstone Motor
notes: &fA steady 1-Power source that runs on its own — no fuel needed.
&fInverted redstone: it runs while UNpowered and switches OFF when you give it a redstone signal, so you can gate it with a lever or clock.
&7Expensive to craft, but maintenance-free once placed.

items.name: &cRedstone Dynamo
notes: &fMeasures the rotation network it's wired into and emits an analog 0-15 redstone signal — read it with a comparator against any side.
&fRight-click to pick what it reports (total / used / unused power) and how it scales to 0-15 (clamp / mod-15 / ÷15).
&fTransmits rotation along its axis like a shaft, and draws no power itself.
&7Wrench: show network debug info.

items.name: &cThrottle Lever
notes: &fA set-and-forget analog redstone source: right-click to raise the output, sneak-right-click to lower it (0-15).
&fPowers adjacent redstone directly (weighted-plate rules) — run dust/lamps against it.
&7Ignores footsteps: stepping on it will not change the signal.

items.name: &fOak Mechanical Casing
notes: &fA frame block: auto-glues only to adjacent frame blocks of the SAME wood (casings, gearboxes, chassis) — build a rigid frame with no glue brush.
&7A plain block never drags it: it rides a mechanism when mounted on it, bonded to a same-wood frame, or pinned with the glue brush.
&7The glue brush pins it to anything — a different wood, or a plain block — overriding the same-wood auto-glue.
&7Comes in every plank wood — the center plank of the recipe picks the variant.

items.name: &fOak Mechanical Chassis
notes: &fA super-casing: grabs every adjacent MOVABLE block except honey (slime parity) — a moving chassis drags its whole payload, no glue brush.
&7Wood-picky for frames: it joins casings, gearboxes and chassis of the SAME wood only, and ignores a different-wood frame.
&7A plain block never drags the chassis itself; a vanilla piston moves a lone chassis as an ordinary block.
&7Craft by ringing a Mechanical Casing with iron nuggets — the casing's wood picks the variant.

items.name: &7Millstone
lore: &7Grinds items from its storage when powered
&7Powered from the top; grinds faster with more power; outputs below
notes: &fGrinds items from its own storage while powered by a shaft on top, dropping the results into a container below it.
&7Grinds more per cycle the more surplus power the network has, up to a cap.

items.name: &fExtractor Press
lore: &7Presses items from its storage when powered
&7Powered from the top; squeezes out juices, oils & extracts below
notes: &fSqueezes items from its storage while powered by a shaft on top, dropping the results into a container below.
&fThis is how you make the juices, oils, and extracts (like Sweet Berry Juice and Seed Oil) — see its recipes below.
&7Presses more per cycle the more surplus power the network has, up to a cap.

items.name: &6Sieve
lore: &7Pans items from its storage when powered — needs water
&7Powered from the top; sifts gravel & sand for nuggets, flint & finds below
notes: &fPans gravel, sand, red sand, dirt, and soul sand from its storage while powered by a shaft on top, dropping any finds into a container below.
&fEvery find is chance-based — a cycle can wash an input away with nothing to show. Gravel is the ore-panning feedstock; sand is the fine-panning gamble.
&fPanning needs WATER: right-click with a water bucket to fill its tank (or feed it by liquid pipe). It sips a bucket every so many pans and idles dry with a dusty rattle.
&7Right-click with an empty hand to read the tank level.

items.name: &bCopper Water Pump
lore: &7Pumps a bucket of water upward each cycle when powered
&7Driven by a shaft through it; wrench flips the flow
notes: &fSits over its water: drains the source block, cauldron, or tank below and discharges one bucket per cycle to the block or pipe network above.
&fPipes route the water to the first vessel that can take it — every pipe along the way must connect. Water only: it will not lift lava.
&7Driven by a shaft running straight through it (the axle lies across your view as you place it); a wrench reverses the flow direction.

items.name: &cBurner
lore: &7Burns fuel to heat a boiler placed on top
&7Bottom of the steam stack: burner, boiler, steam piston
notes: &fThe firebox of the steam engine: load it with fuel (coal, wood, lava buckets — anything the engine burns) and stack a [Boiler](mech:boiler) and [Steam Piston](mech:steam_piston) on top.
&7Right-click to open its fuel storage and read the remaining burn time.

items.name: &fBoiler
lore: &7Boils piped-in water over a burner; a steam piston on top makes power
&7Middle of the steam stack: burner, boiler, steam piston
notes: &fHolds the steam engine's water: stack it on a [Burner](mech:burner), put a [Steam Piston](mech:steam_piston) on top, and keep it fed — by [Copper Water Pump](mech:pump) and pipes, or by hand with water buckets.
&7The running stack sips a bucket of water roughly every minute and stops dry.

items.name: &fSteam Piston
lore: &720 Power while its boiler and burner below are fed
&7Top of the steam stack; drives shafts along its axle
notes: &fThe strongest power source: stack it on a [Boiler](mech:boiler) over a [Burner](mech:burner), feed fuel and water, and it drives 20 Power into shafts on both sides of its axle.
&7The axle lies across your view as you place it; a wrench reads out the network.

items.name: &aBlock Placer
lore: &7Places blocks from its storage in front when powered
&7Powered by a shaft (from the top, or any side on a ceiling)
notes: &fMounts on a wall over a container and places its stored blocks into the space in front of it, one per cycle, while powered by a shaft on top.
&fCan also mount on a ceiling: it pulls from the container above and places into the cell below, powered from any side.
&7Vanilla blocks only — it skips custom plugin blocks and anything that isn't a placeable block.

items.name: &cMechanical Dispenser
notes: &fWorks exactly like a vanilla dispenser until you feed it rotation power from any side.
&fPowered, it launches arrows and items harder and straighter — extra speed scales with the network's total power, up to a cap.
&fDispensed TNT is thrown forward instead of dropping in place.
&7Wrench: show network debug info.

items.name: &8Drill
notes: &fMounts on any face — wall, floor, or ceiling — and breaks the block directly in front of it while it has power.
&fThe drill face is the face you click when placing — it mines away from that face.
&7Breaking runs in stages (like real mining), so harder blocks take longer to pop.
&7Mount it on a rotator to sweep-mine an arc: it bores at any angle through the swing, at 2× speed since it only grazes each block.
&cWon't break: bedrock, spawners, reinforced deepslate, and moving pistons.

items.name: &aWindmill
lore: &7Use Large/Huge banners for a bigger windmill
notes: &fA passive power source — it spins on its own, with no fuel or redstone needed.
&fThe banner patterns from the four banners you craft it with show up on the blades, so a dyed/patterned banner makes a custom windmill.
&7Craft with plain banners for this tier; use Large or Huge banners to get the Large/Huge Windmill instead.
&7Places on the floor or a ceiling (spins flat, either way) or on a wall (spins like a wheel).

items.name: &2Large Windmill
lore: &7Crafted like a Windmill using Large banners
notes: &fThe 5-Power tier: same recipe as the Windmill, but with four Large Banners in place of plain banners.
&fBlades are 3x the size of a plain Windmill's and still carry the banners' patterns.
&fA passive source — spins on its own, no fuel or redstone.
&7Banner tiers require the [BetterBanners](https://modrinth.com/plugin/betterbanners) plugin.

items.name: &bHuge Windmill
lore: &7Crafted like a Windmill using Huge banners
notes: &fThe biggest tier at 15 Power: same recipe as the Windmill, but with four Huge Banners.
&fBlades are the largest of the three tiers and still show the banners' patterns.
&fA passive source — spins on its own, no fuel or redstone.
&7Banner tiers require the [BetterBanners](https://modrinth.com/plugin/betterbanners) plugin.

items.name: &fFan
lore: &7Pushes mobs, players & items away from its mount
&7Stronger with more surplus power; fixed range
notes: &fBlows a straight beam of wind out of its face, pushing mobs, players, and dropped items along it.
&fPlace it on the floor to blow things upward, or on a wall to blow them outward.
&7Reaches a fixed distance (about 5 blocks); it does not push farther with more power.
&7Extra surplus power on the network makes the push stronger, up to a cap — it doesn't extend the range.

items.name: &bSuction Hopper
lore: &7Pulls nearby dropped items inward while powered
&7Captures them and feeds the container it's mounted on
&7Powered from any side that isn't its mount
notes: &fWhile powered it sucks dropped items from a 3×3×3 area into itself, then pushes them into the container it's placed on (below on the floor, or into the wall).
&fUnlike most machines it takes rotation power from a shaft on any of its five open faces.
&fIt feeds vanilla containers directly, and also pushes into a pipe mounted below it (when the Pipes plugin is present).
&7With no container to output into, it just holds the items in its own inventory.

items.name: &6Mechanical Minecart
lore: &7Right-click a rail to spawn a cart.
&7Glue blocks to it, then power an
notes: &fRight-click a rail to spawn a cart, then glue blocks onto it with the [Glue Brush](mech:glue_item).
&fPush it onto a powered activator rail (or right-click the cart) to assemble the glued blocks into a rideable moving structure; another activator rail disassembles it back into blocks.
&7It's an item you use on a rail, not a block you place in the world.

items.name: &bPiston Core
lore: &7Spin CW to extend, CCW to retract
notes: &fThe powered base of a mechanical piston. Feed it rotational power from any side.
&7Build a line of piston poles through it, capped by a piston head; reach = poles behind the core.
&7Placement decides 'forward' — the direction it pushes.

items.name: &bPiston Head
lore: &7The pushing face at the end of the rod

items.name: &bPropeller
notes: &fA powered propeller. Point it along a ship to go faster, across it to turn quicker, or
&fmount it flat to push the ship up.
&7Draws 5 power while running — it produces none.
&7Craft from a Windmill; its blades carry over.
&7Places on the floor or a ceiling (spins flat, either way) or on a wall (spins like a wheel).

items.name: &bLarge Propeller
notes: &fA powered propeller. Point it along a ship to go faster, across it to turn quicker, or
&fmount it flat to push the ship up.
&7Draws 10 power while running — it produces none.
&7Craft from a Large Windmill; its blades carry over.
&7Places on the floor or a ceiling (spins flat, either way) or on a wall (spins like a wheel).

items.name: &bHuge Propeller
notes: &fA powered propeller. Point it along a ship to go faster, across it to turn quicker, or
&fmount it flat to push the ship up.
&7Draws 20 power while running — it produces none.
&7Craft from a Huge Windmill; its blades carry over.
&7Places on the floor or a ceiling (spins flat, either way) or on a wall (spins like a wheel).

items.name: &cThruster
notes: &fA fuel-burning rocket. Feed it coal, charcoal, blaze rods or lava like an engine.
&fMounted on the floor or ceiling it fires downward and lifts a ship; on a wall it drives
&fthe ship along or turns it, depending which way it faces.
&7It produces no rotational power — it only pushes.
&7It burns only while a moving ship uses it; placed on its own it burns nothing.
&7Craft from a Fan, four iron ingots, two blaze rods and a blast furnace.

items.name: &dReaction Wheel
lore: &7Turns a ship faster, even at a standstill
notes: &fA heavy spinning disc. Drive it from a shaft underneath.
&fOn a ship it improves turning only — it will not make you go faster or lift you.
&7Works at a standstill, unlike sails — but so does a propeller mounted across the hull,
&7and that turns far harder. This is the cheap option: one power against a propeller's five,
&7and the only turning you can get out of a floor mount.
&7Floor placement only.
&7Craft from two redstone, an iron block and a bearing.

items.name: &fOak Wheel
notes: &fA powered wheel. Mount it on the left or right side of a vehicle; wheels on the front
&for back face do nothing. Powered wheels drive the vehicle on land; unpowered ones still roll.
&fIt takes power through the block it hangs on: run a shaft or engine along its axle.
&7Draws 2 power, only while its vehicle is assembled — a placed wheel draws none and stays still.
&7Climbs steps up to 1 block high. The tyre reaches 0 blocks below the block it hangs on.
&7Craft from a Rotator with four oak planks around it.
&7Wall placement only.

items.name: &fLarge Oak Wheel
notes: &fA powered wheel. Mount it on the left or right side of a vehicle; wheels on the front
&for back face do nothing. Powered wheels drive the vehicle on land; unpowered ones still roll.
&fIt takes power through the block it hangs on: run a shaft or engine along its axle.
&7Draws 5 power, only while its vehicle is assembled — a placed wheel draws none and stays still.
&7Climbs steps up to 1.5 blocks high. The tyre reaches 0.5 blocks below the block it hangs on.
&7Craft from a Oak Wheel with four oak planks around it.
&7Wall placement only.

items.name: &fHuge Oak Wheel
notes: &fA powered wheel. Mount it on the left or right side of a vehicle; wheels on the front
&for back face do nothing. Powered wheels drive the vehicle on land; unpowered ones still roll.
&fIt takes power through the block it hangs on: run a shaft or engine along its axle.
&7Draws 10 power, only while its vehicle is assembled — a placed wheel draws none and stays still.
&7Climbs steps up to 2 blocks high. The tyre reaches 1 block below the block it hangs on.
&7Craft from a Large Oak Wheel with four oak planks around it.
&7Wall placement only.

items.name: &dSweet Berry Juice
notes: &fMade by pressing sweet berries in the Extractor Press.
&7It's a Potion of Instant Health under the hood — drink it to heal.

items.name: &eSeed Oil
notes: &fMade by pressing seeds in the [Extractor Press](mech:press).
&7Burn it in the [Engine](mech:engine) as fuel, or craft it with a string and
&7iron/copper nuggets into a lantern.

items.name: &fFlour
notes: &fGrind wheat in the [Millstone](mech:millstone) — 2 flour per wheat.
&7Combine 3 flour + a water bucket into [Dough](mech:dough), then bake it into bread.

items.name: &eDough
notes: &fCraft 3 [Flour](mech:flour) + a water bucket into dough (keeps the bucket).
&7Smelt dough in a furnace or smoker to bake it into bread.

items.name: &aSugarcane Juice
notes: &fPress sugarcane in the [Extractor Press](mech:press) to bottle it.
&7Drink it for a short Speed boost.

items.name: &6Glow Berry Juice
lore: &7Drink to give off a soft glow
notes: &fPress glow berries in the [Extractor Press](mech:press).
&7Drink it to glow for a while.

items.name: &7Bearing
notes: &fThe core component most rotation machines are built from — windmills, the fan, the clutch, the engine, and more all need one.
&7Craft a batch of these first when starting a mechanism build.

items.name: &6Rotation Wrench
notes: &fRight-click a rotation machine to read its network info — power, connections, and spin direction.
&fSome machines have a custom wrench action (a power source flips its spin direction). It never rotates or re-aims a machine.
&7Unbreakable — one wrench lasts forever.

items.name: &aGlue Brush
lore: &7Right-click a hinge or minecart to edit
&7Right-click air: reset corner  ·  Sneak-right hinge: clear
notes: &fThe authoring tool for moving structures: use it to pick exactly which blocks a [Rotator](mech:rotator) or [Mechanical Minecart](mech:mechanism_minecart) carries.
&7Glue a selection to a hinge or cart and it moves those blocks as one; see the controls above.
&8It's a real brush and wears down one durability per block you glue.

items.name: &6Coal Minecart
lore: &7Right-click a rail to spawn a fuel tender.
&7Feeds furnace & blast-furnace carts in its train.
&7Accepts only fuel; hoppers above/beside fill it.
notes: &fRight-click a rail to spawn a coal tender: a minecart with a 9-slot, fuel-only inventory rendered as a block of coal.
&fCouple it into a train and it automatically feeds any furnace or blast-furnace cart in that train.
&7Hoppers above or beside the track can refill it as it passes.

items.name: &cBlast Furnace Minecart
lore: &7Right-click a rail to spawn a fast locomotive.
&7Three fuel slots, plus in-GUI - / + buttons that
&7set its cruise speed. Much higher top speed.
notes: &fRight-click a rail to spawn a blast-furnace locomotive: a fuel cart with three fuel slots and in-GUI - / + speed buttons that set a cruise speed (like a controller rail, in redstone steps), plus a far higher configurable top speed.
&fPowers a whole train from anywhere in the consist.

items.name: &bDispenser Minecart
lore: &7Right-click a rail to spawn a dispenser cart.
&7Fires one item upward each time it rolls
notes: &fRight-click a rail to spawn a dispenser minecart: a 3×3 inventory that launches one item straight up every time it crosses a powered activator rail.
&7Hoppers above/beside the track load it; unlike the fuel carts it accepts any item.

items.name: &eMinecart Junction
lore: &7A crossing rail: a cart passing over it keeps
&7its heading and goes straight instead of curving.
notes: &fPlace where two straight tracks cross. A cart crossing it continues straight in the direction it was already travelling, so north–south and east–west lines can intersect without turning carts.

items.name: &cDestructor Rail
lore: &7Destroys any minecart that passes over it,
&7depositing the cart item and its contents into
&7the container directly below (else on the ground).
notes: &fA detector rail that recycles a passing minecart: it ejects any riders, then drops the cart item, everything in its inventory, and any coupling chains into the barrel / dropper / dispenser directly below — or onto the ground if there is no container.
&7Mechanical minecarts are exempt and pass over unharmed.

items.name: &aController Rail
lore: &7Sets the target speed of a fueled blast-furnace
&7cart passing over it, from its redstone signal:
&7No effect on trains without a lit blast cart.
notes: &fA rail that sets the cruise speed of a passing blast-furnace locomotive by its redstone signal strength: 0 → stop, 15 → full speed, linear between. The train accelerates or brakes toward that target and holds it even after leaving the rail — place another controller to set a new one.

&7Build a RUN of these — braking is gradual (~13 blocks to stop from full), so a single rail barely changes speed; a zone of unpowered controllers makes a stop-and-hold station that departs when re-powered.
&7Only affects a train that has a lit (fueled) blast-furnace cart.

items.name: &6Copper Pipe
lore: &7Pulls items out of the container or pipe it is placed on.

items.name: &7Iron Pipe
lore: &7Pulls items out of the container or pipe it is placed on.

items.name: &eGold Pipe
lore: &7Pulls items out of the container or pipe it is placed on.

items.name: &2Oxidized Copper Pipe
lore: &7Pulls items out of the container or pipe it is placed on.

items.name: &6Copper Filter Pipe
lore: &7Pulls only the items you allow out of the container behind it.

items.name: &7Iron Filter Pipe
lore: &7Pulls only the items you allow out of the container behind it.
&7Right-click to set the filter and whitelist/blacklist mode.

items.name: &eGold Filter Pipe
lore: &7Pulls only the items you allow out of the container behind it.
&7Right-click to set the filter, mode, and exact/material matching.

items.name: &6Copper Corner Pipe
lore: &7Pushes items toward the block it was placed against.
&7Must have another pipe feeding into it.

items.name: &7Iron Corner Pipe
lore: &7Pushes items toward the block it was placed against.
&7Must have another pipe feeding into it.

items.name: &eGold Corner Pipe
lore: &7Pushes items toward the block it was placed against.
&7Must have another pipe feeding into it.

items.name: &2Oxidized Copper Corner Pipe
lore: &7Pushes items toward the block it was placed against.
&7Must have another pipe feeding into it.

items.name: &fLarge Banner
lore: &7Place a banner in the center, surround with wool.

items.name: &fHuge Banner
lore: &7Place a large banner in the center, surround with wool.
